title: Source-release refresh + re-validation process
context: Track packs are versioned to their source release — when a source publishes a new release (e.g. a new GENCODE version or a CIViC data dump), the affected packs may become stale or incorrect. Without a documented refresh process, packs silently age. M3 requires a documented source-release refresh process and a named steward for ongoing liaison, so stale packs are caught and re-validated as maintenance tasks rather than silently left in place.
objective: Document the source-release refresh process: how to detect a source's new release, which packs are affected, how to re-validate (re-run gates + validators + render check), and how stale packs become maintenance tasks.
acceptanceCriteria: Documents the detection step: how to monitor each approved source for new releases (e.g. GitHub releases, FTP changelogs, NCBI announcements) and how to determine which packs are affected.

Documents the re-validation procedure: re-run licensegate-002 and coordgate-003, rebuild track files, re-run validateFiles/hubCheck, and re-execute the render check — producing updated gate artifacts.
Documents how a stale pack transitions to a maintenance task in the backlog, with the old version deprecated and the new version noted.
Names the Steward responsible for monitoring source releases and initiating refresh tasks.
Document output licensed CC-BY-4.0; commit is DCO signed-off.
resources: PLAN.md (Risk table — source release changes annotations)
output: review/refresh-022-process.md — committed source-release refresh process document with named steward and per-source monitoring checklist.
